OBJECTIVES
What the project set out to do
TimetableMaster · Final Year Project
3
▪ Generate clash-free timetables automatically from a curriculum
▪ Respect every hard rule: rooms, availability, workload caps, two-week A/B cycles
▪ Keep human judgement: drag & drop edits that survive regeneration (pinned lessons)
▪ Handle day-2 operations: leave workflow, ranked cover suggestions, school calendar
▪ Make the result usable: CSV / PDF / ICS export, read-only share links, notifications
▪ Make it accountable and safe: role-based access, multi-tenancy, activity log
▪ Prove it works: automated tests at three layers, run in CI on every push

TECHNICAL CORE
The scheduling engine: rules that must never break
TimetableMaster · Final Year Project
6
HARD CONSTRAINTS — never violated
▪ A class, a teacher and a room host at most one lesson per period
▪ Teachers are only scheduled inside their availability
▪ Lesson max-per-day; teacher daily and weekly workload caps
▪ Fixed rooms must match; required room types must fit the class
▪ Hand-pinned lessons stay exactly where they are
SOFT GOALS — optimised
▪ No gaps in a class's day; no gaps in a teacher's day
▪ The same subject is spread across the week, not clustered
▪ Teacher load is balanced across days
▪ Work is balanced across the cycle weeks (A/B)
▪ Weights are tunable per run through the API
HOW THE SOLVER WORKS
Two phases, deterministic, and it explains itself
TimetableMaster · Final Year Project
7
1
Greedy seeding
Most-constrained-first: the lessons with the fewest legal slots are placed first, so the search space never closes unnecessarily.
2
Simulated annealing
Relocate / swap / insert moves explore neighbouring solutions and accept worse ones at high temperature to escape local optima.
3
Report
Placed periods, unplaced periods with the dominant reason (teacher unavailable / busy / limits / room), moves and quality score.
Determinism is a tested property: the same seed and iteration count produce the same timetable — 12 unit tests cover feasibility, clashes, limits, room rules, pinned placements and two-week cycles.

NON-FUNCTIONAL
Security, roles and accountability
TimetableMaster · Final Year Project
14
Passwords
argon2 hashing; the demo school is rebuildable in one click
Sessions
HS256 JWTs signed with a per-installation secret (auto-generated on first run)
Authorisation
every write endpoint requires admin or scheduler; teachers request leave only for themselves; students are read-only
Tenancy
every row is school-scoped from the token — no cross-school reads
Public links
unguessable tokens, revocable, return 404 the moment they are revoked
Audit
generation, edits, cover decisions and account changes are all logged with actor and timestamp

A BUG ONLY THE SUITE COULD FIND
CI reported green while the runner was silently testing a stale server left behind by an earlier run — it killed a shell instead of the process. The runner now execs the server, refuses to start when the port is already answering, and prints every check it ran.

NEXT STEPS
Limitations & future work
TimetableMaster · Final Year Project
17
KNOWN LIMITATIONS
▪ SQLite keeps the app single-node; no horizontal write scaling
▪ No teacher/team-taught lessons yet — one teacher per lesson
▪ Subject-vs-time-of-day preferences are not modelled
▪ Solver quality is bounded by the time budget, not proven optimal
NEXT STEPS
▪ Multi-teacher lessons and lab/elective slots
▪ iCal subscription feed (the one-off .ics export already exists)
▪ Postgres + container deployment for multi-school districts
▪ Compare against an off-the-shelf CP-SAT solver as a benchmark
